title: Thursday Teacher Plan
note: Blooket opener. One turn-in per class: the exit ticket. Build day for 8th, Test 1 for 7th, tactical fix for 6th.

4th Period.topic: Strategy pattern, Day 4: build the moving brick
4th Period.goal: By the end of class, my live game has at least one row of bricks using my slide strategy, and every other brick uses stayStill.
4th Period.exitTicket: What did you build today, and where does your strategy run every frame?
prep: Day 4 handout attached to Strategy Pattern; exit ticket posted
Your own Codespace ready to demo the prompt (don't commit your demo to a student repo)

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Wednesday: swap slide for stayStill, the loop never changes, tracing x.
tips: Load the Blooket_*_Thu_Nov5 set before the bell.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed questions, then read the goal: By the end of class, my live game has at least one row of bricks using my slide strategy, and every other brick uses stayStill.
tips: Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: I do: the 3 pieces
segments.do: Walk the table: two strategies in bricks.js; move/speed/startX in the brick factory; brick.move(brick) loop in update(). Show the prompt and its 2 blanks.
segments.why: Students know what to look for before Copilot writes anything.
tips: Ask: which piece never changes when you swap?

segments.title: You do: prompt + check
segments.do: Fill in row and speed from Tuesday's exit ticket, paste into Copilot Chat, find all 3 pieces in the changes, then Keep.
tips: Lost plan: row 0, speed 1.
Overlapping bricks = Copilot bounced off walls; re-prompt with startX.
'brick.move is not a function' = some bricks missing move.

segments.title: Commit, sync, refresh, play
segments.do: Source Control, commit message, Commit, Sync Changes, wait 1 min, open the Pages link, Ctrl+Shift+R, play.
segments.why: The long chain is where students drop off; do it together.
tips: Count down each step on the board.
Blank screen: F12 console, paste the error into Copilot.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: On Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Full answer: names the row given slide and says it runs inside update() (brick.move(brick)) every frame.

watchFor: Students who never commit/sync: their live game won't change.
Copilot rewriting unrelated code: Undo and re-paste.
Students stuck >3 min on the chain: pair with a neighbor who finished.

6th Period.topic: Warren Truss Build, Day 4: Test 1 (one strike)
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, my group predicted, then tested our bridge with water bottles and marked exactly where it failed first.
6th Period.exitTicket: Where did your bridge fail first, and why do you think it failed there?
prep: Day 4 handout attached to the exit ticket
About 5 full 16.9 oz water bottles per group
Test stations: 2 desks a 1-stick gap apart; backpacks/jackets under

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Wednesday: deck tabs on the outside, faces not edges, deck at the bottom joints, cross pieces.
tips: Load the Blooket_*_Thu_Nov5 set before the bell.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed questions, then read the goal: By the end of class, my group predicted, then tested our bridge with water bottles and marked exactly where it failed first.
tips: Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Roles + the 5 rules
segments.do: Youngest Loader, 2nd youngest Spotter, 2nd oldest Recorder, oldest Checker. Bottles count as materials under the one-strike rules.
segments.why: Clear limits before bottles come out.

segments.title: Set up + predict
segments.do: Bridge across the 1-stick gap, 1/4 stick on each desk; platform (1/2 x 1/2 stick) on the deck over the 2 middle bottom joints. Recorder writes the prediction on the label.

segments.title: Test 1
segments.do: One bottle on its side at a time, wait 5 s, Checker says go; STOP at the first crack, lean, sag or popped joint. Recorder writes Test 1: N bottles and marks an X.
segments.why: Analyze: find the weak spot for Friday's plan.
tips: Spotter hovers, never touches.
Groups done early: look closely at every joint near the X and name the failure type (popped, bent, torn, leaned, sagged).

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: On Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Full answer: a spot plus a reason (glue let go, edge joint, deck bent between joints, piece bent).

segments.title: Clean up
segments.do: Bottles back, bridges on the shelf with the label.
tips: The Test 1 number must be on the label for Friday's Answers page.

watchFor: Rule breaks: call it at once, calmly.

7th Period.topic: Bridge Load Test, Day 4: fix the weak spot
7th Period.goal: By the end of class, my group has a plan for up to 6 tactical popsicle sticks and has added them exactly where our bridge failed in Test 1.
7th Period.exitTicket: Predict Test 2: how many bottles will your bridge hold now, and why?
prep: Day 4 handout attached to Bridge Deck and Load Test
6 popsicle sticks per group (Materials Managers count them out)
Joints That Hold cards, scrap paper for wraps, glue sticks, scissors. No tape.
Bridges with X marks and Test 1 numbers handed back

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Wednesday: STOP at the first crack, the X, predicting, the test setup.
tips: Load the Blooket_*_Thu_Nov5 set before the bell.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed questions, then read the goal: By the end of class, my group has a plan for up to 6 tactical popsicle sticks and has added them exactly where our bridge failed in Test 1.
tips: Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Roles by birthday
segments.do: Youngest Planner, 2nd youngest Builder, 2nd oldest Materials Manager, oldest Checker. Group of 3: Checker also MM. Group of 5: two Builders.

segments.title: What kind of failure?
segments.do: Walk the failure table: popped joint, bent (squeezed), torn (pulled), leaned, sagged, and the matching fix. Each group names theirs.
segments.why: Diagnosis before treatment: rigor for this class.
tips: Bent = compression/buckling; torn = tension. Use the words squeezed and pulled.

segments.title: Repair + plan
segments.do: Re-glue what broke. Planner dots where each stick goes (max 6, each touching the X or the failed piece); Checker approves.
tips: Push back on sticks far from the X: why there?

segments.title: You do: glue tactical sticks
segments.do: Each stick glued flat against a cardboard face, never on an edge; paper-wrap both ends; press 30 s. MM writes Sticks added: N on the label.
tips: Praise groups that use fewer sticks precisely.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: On Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Full answer: a number of bottles plus the fix location as the reason.

segments.title: Clean up + dry overnight
segments.do: Bridges flat on the shelf; no testing today.
segments.why: Glue needs to set before Test 2.

accommodations: Goal reviewed after the Blooket and at the exit ticket; numbered steps; worked examples (Copilot prompt, test diagram, failure table); two sentence frames.
Pictures for key words (strategy, commit; platform, fail; squeezed, pulled, tactical); partner talk before writing.
Lexend Deca; steps read aloud; speech-to-text OK.
Timed chunks with a visual timer; hands-on roles (Loader, Spotter, Builder); the 8th commit chain counted down step by step.
Dictated exit tickets; floors: 8th gets the prompt pasted and Kept; 7th says where it failed; 6th adds 1 stick at the X.
frameworks: 8th makes the feature live; 6th and 7th run real load tests on their own bridges.
Roles with authority: the Checker calls STOP and approves every stick.
The 85 points don't depend on working code; failure in tests is planned and safe.
